description: The sources do not state whether 30-40 tonnes of copper per MW refer to total installed capacity or IT capacity. In the IEA annex IT capacity is 11% to 37% below total capacity depending on case and year (23% in the Base Case in 2030); for the Base Case in 2030 the choice lowers new-capacity copper by 18% and the extra over the base year by 11%

description: S13 reports 1.1 Mt of data-centre copper demand for 2025. The model gives about 0.42-0.56 Mt for the 2024 build (14 GW x 30-40 t/MW), so S13 is about 2.0 to 2.6 times higher. Not reconciled: the definitions may differ (for example installed stock, other equipment, or a different year)
note: Still open. Shown side by side in notebook 03 and not used; S13 is a secondary, low-reliability source

description: The IEA EV data has no hybrid (HEV) split. Hybrids (about 39-45 kg of copper, S11) sit in the non-EV car group, which is treated as 18-22 kg. A bounding case (all non-EV cars at 39-45 kg) is shown instead of a data-based sensitivity
note: A hybrid share of non-EV sales would be needed from another source

description: The IEA file has no 2030 EV projection (2025 actuals and 2035 scenarios only). 2030 is interpolated (straight line and constant growth) and 2035 is shown beside it

IEA numbers are rounded to two significant figures and EV shares to whole percent. Total car sales derived as EV sales / share, and so the growth in total sales, carry a rounding band of several million cars
note: Shown as a band; total sales growth is not from EV data but derived

description: Vans, buses, trucks and 2 and 3-wheelers have no copper intensity in the project data and are excluded; fuel-cell cars are excluded too (about 7,000 sold in 2025). The EV result is therefore understated
